doneEventValidationModel.canonicalShape: A terminal marker is a canonical ads/github DISPATCH_STATE_CHANGED event comment with dispatch_state DONE. It is exact and unedited only when: the canonical comment parse passes unchanged (single marker, byte-stable body, created_at === updated_at); it binds the same native Task Issue; its dispatchId equals the historical candidate's dispatchId; its protectedClaimKey equals the historical candidate's protectedClaimKey; its admission_generation equals the historical candidate's generation; and predecessor_claim_comment_id equals the historical candidate's exact comment id. A DONE binding any other Task, dispatch, key, generation or comment id is invalid, not merely inapplicable.
doneEventValidationModel.filterScope: A legal DONE filters ONLY the historical candidate it exactly binds. It never filters other candidates, never transfers authority, never constitutes a new Claim, and never relaxes any other fail-closed rule.
doneEventValidationModel.editedAndMalformed: Edited DONE bodies (created_at !== updated_at or body hash drift), duplicate dispatch IDs, malformed canonical comments and non-DONE state changes keep today's rejection behavior unchanged.

dualReadback.principle: Native DONE alone is not a new Claim, not admission and not permission. Before a fresh registry is created for a successor, the Host independently reads back the historical CAS row and requires it to be exactly TERMINAL_VERIFIED for the same Task, dispatchId, protectedClaimKey and generation as the DONE binding.
failClosed: Historical row PENDING (including lost-ACK PENDING): BLOCKED; reconcile by readback, never blind POST.
Historical row divergent (different state, task, dispatch, key or generation than the DONE binding): BLOCKED.
Historical row missing / CAS readback unavailable: BLOCKED with UNKNOWN preserved distinguishable from FAILED.
dualReadback.readModel: Reads go through public DomainHarness CAS store APIs under the real Host fence; never raw SQLite, never fixture authority.

freshSuccessorRules: A fresh successor uses a NEW dispatch ID (never the historical dispatch:219:maintenance:20261031:1) and a FRESH DEDICATED registry.
A fresh successor never rewrites, aliases, seeds from or deletes the historical row; the historical registry row and its comment are immutable history.
A fresh successor never edits or replaces the historical DISPATCH_CLAIMED comment and never publishes a second maintenance Issue; #220 stays the one real #219 maintenance Issue.

The terminalized historical Claim does not count as an active incompatible role in the merged #414 role-compatibility model; a distinct role remains admissible and the same role remains a duplicate denial unless it is the fresh successor itself.

Fresh admission still requires the full existing surface: open/type:task/state:ready/CLEAR/zero open blockers preflight, canonical key and generation binding, protected-claim-key uniqueness in the new registry, exact native comment/CAS readback and FSW creation.
